summary: Post-deploy safety sanity check: combined quant + large batching + KV-prefetch caused tail latency spikes and intermittent 5xx
description:
Issue summary:
Customer applied a combined optimization profile that enabled an aggressive quantization variant (gptj-6b-quant-v2), increased target_batch_size to 256, and turned on KV-prefetch (kv_prefetch=true) across their dedicated pool. Within 20 minutes they observed a 3x increase in 99th-percentile latency, sporadic 5xx responses for generation requests, and a rise in token-level decoding errors (invalid token sequences).

Impact:
- Several production endpoints returned intermittent 500/502 for ~10% of requests during peak windows.
- 99p latency regressed from ~210ms to ~750ms.
- Customer user-facing errors and queueing leading to increased error budget usage.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: df-prod-dedicated-7 (us-east)
- Model variants: gptj-6b-quant-v2 (rolled out via optimize profile), fallback gptj-6b-vanilla-v1
- Client traffic: steady QPS ~120, 90% short responses (<128 tokens)
- Feature flags: optimize_profile=v2026-03-10-hybrid

Steps to reproduce (as observed by customer):
1) Send concurrent generation requests to model endpoint pinned to optimize_profile v2026-03-10-hybrid.
2) Observe elevated queueing and occasional 5xx in response stream.
3) Reduce concurrency and errors drop.

Observed metrics and traces:
- 5xx rate spiked to 9% for the dedicated pool between 15:20-15:45 UTC.
- CPU/GPU utilization remained high but not saturated (GPU 68-75%).
- Memory fragmentation and occasional OOM events on a subset of nodes (node ids in logs).
- Traces show long tail in scheduler wait time and repeated kernel selection retries for quant kernels.

Logs (redacted snippets):
[2026-03-10T15:21:12Z] worker-27 WARN kernel_selector: quant-kernel-fallback triggered for model=gptj-6b-quant-v2 seq_len=128
[2026-03-10T15:21:15Z] worker-27 ERROR runtime: decode_error token_seq_mismatch request_id=abcd-1234
[2026-03-10T15:23:48Z] scheduler WARN request_queue: delayed_by_ms=482 provider=dedicated-pool-df-prod-dedicated-7

Temporary mitigation requested: Customer asked for a safe, stepwise rollback of the optimization profile and guidance on guardrails to avoid reintroducing the issue when tuning again.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Enable hybrid optimize_profile that sets quant_variant=gptj-6b-quant-v2, target_batch_size=256, kv_prefetch=true. 2) Route steady production traffic (~100-150 QPS) to the dedicated pool. 3) Watch 99p latency and 5xx counts within 10-30 minutes.
logs: See snippets in description. Full logs attached by customer via secure upload (s3://redwood-secure-uploads/textforge/2026-03-10/logs.zip). Relevant grep: 'quant-kernel-fallback', 'decode_error', 'delayed_by_ms'.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: incompatibility between aggressive quant kernel selection and KV-prefetch leading to increased kernel selection retries and memory fragmentation. Support ran quick checks: 1) Verified that the quant variant uses a different attention kernel path that allocates ephemeral per-request buffers; 2) KV-prefetch duplicates KV caches ahead of schedule which increases transient GPU memory pressure when combined with large batches; 3) Scheduler observed longer lock contention when many large-batch requests hit the same worker.

Additional findings:
- Node-level logs show repeated freeing/alloc of device buffers around kernel fallback events.
- Trace correlation: requests that hit kernel fallback had ~4x higher decode errors.
- Not all nodes affected—pattern aligns to a subset with older driver (nvidia-driver 470.x) where a quant kernel had a regression.

Actions taken so far:
- Scoped traffic away from the most-affected nodes via fleet labeling (partial mitigation).
- Disabled kv_prefetch for the customer's optimize_profile as an immediate safe rollback step (applied 2026-03-10T16:05Z).
- Lowered global target_batch_size cap for the customer's pool from 256 to 64 as interim.
comments: Priya Malhotra (Support) 2026-03-10: Logged issue after customer reported. Requested logs, profile config, and peak QPS. Asked SRE to check node health.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Noted driver mismatch on 3 nodes (nvidia-driver 470.161). Marking nodes for cordon and drain for investigation. Suggested disabling kv_prefetch as safe immediate mitigation.

Maya Chen (Customer Engineer) 2026-03-10: Customer confirms rollback of kv_prefetch reduced 5xx to <1% within 10 minutes but 99p latency still elevated (~370ms). Requests recommended stepwise rollback checklist.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-11: Identified PR that fixed quant kernel memory allocation behavior: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1894. Patch scheduled for canary rollout after validation of drivers.
Priya Malhotra (Support) 2026-03-12: Sent customer the safe rollback checklist and asked for approval to pin model variant to gptj-6b-vanilla-v1 while patch rolls out. Customer agreed.
TextForge Labs (Customer) 2026-03-12: Approved temporary pin and asked for post-mortem and configuration guardrails before re-enabling hybrid profile.
recommended_action:
Stepwise safe rollback/guardrails to provide to customer: 
1) Pin model to known-good variant: set model_pin=gptj-6b-vanilla-v1 for the customer's endpoint (immediate).
2) Revert kv_prefetch to false in optimize_profile and wait 15 minutes to observe error rate drop (already done).
3) Reduce target_batch_size cap to 32 for customer pool; monitor 99p latency and GPU memory pressure.
4) Only re-enable single optimization at a time: first reintroduce a conservative quant profile with quant_variant=gptj-6b-quant-v1 and batch cap 32, observe for 4 hours; then test kv_prefetch with low prefetch window.
5) Verify all nodes are on driver >= 515.x before enabling quant-optimized kernels cluster-wide.
6) If kernel-fallback events reappear, disable quant kernels via feature gate: feature.quant_kernels.enabled=false for the pool and open an ops-run to backfill the patch.

We recommended a staged dry-run on a shadow traffic subset before full rollouts.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: kv_prefetch disabled and model pinned to gptj-6b-vanilla-v1. Batch size cap lowered to 64, then to 32 after observation. Full fix pending canary of runtime PR and driver upgrades. Customer agreed to staged re-testing and requested a short post-mortem once rollout completes.
follow_up_items: 1) Track canary rollout of PR #1894 and driver upgrades (owner: Diego). 2) Run a short postmortem and share in confluence page linked above (owner: Priya). 3) Add a safety gate to optimize-tooling: block hybrid profile enables if fleet has nodes with driver <515 (owner: Optimize team).
customer_notes: Customer appreciated quick rollback assistance. They requested an explicit checklist to avoid reintroducing combined changes and asked for a pre-check tool in the console to flag risky combos (large batch + kv_prefetch + quant on older drivers).
postmortem_plan: If canary validates, produce a 1-page postmortem summarizing root cause (quant kernel allocation + kv-prefetch memory pressure + old driver regression), timeline, and preventive actions. Share with customer and internal SRE/opt teams.
communication_log: Support updated customer 2026-03-11 18:10 UTC: kv_prefetch rolled back; 5xx dropped. 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC: model pinned. 2026-03-13 14:00 UTC: SRE scheduled canary for PR #1894.
